entries.environment: Final source in Chrome through the local PlayDrop SDK harness, plus deterministic Playwright mechanics proof and PlayDrop project validation
entries.surface: Chrome portrait window 533x806; automated primary-surface coverage at 390x844; desktop is compatibility-only
actions: Loaded the final build directly into the authored endless opening in a portrait Chrome window.
Tapped once and observed the real chopping-knife GLB rotate blade-up/forward into the wall.
Observed seven geometrically reached brick courses score one point each while untouched courses remained intact.
Observed bright per-course interior caps, restrained opposing fragment motion, and a delayed NICE callout after the blade cleared.
Staged an isolated handle-only target contact and observed zero score, zero split targets, and a visible upward/backward bounce.
statesObserved: Textured PlayDrop chopping-knife GLB centered on the course lane
Blade and handle collision regions resolved per physical target using previous, midpoint, and current contact order
A handle-first contact cannot score or create split geometry
A normal opening strike cuts exactly seven courses and preserves forward rotation
Untouched wall courses remain visible and collidable
Each accepted course emits an individual +1 and exposes a saturated interior cap
Fourteen physical wall halves separate, fall forward, contact platforms or ground, and settle without fragment-to-fragment explosions
Repeated taps add bounded lift and rotation without stair-stepping above the course
Portrait gameplay fills the automated 390x844 canvas and the Chrome portrait window
Final Chrome replay produced no uncaught console errors
consoleWarnings: Rapier compatibility initializer reports its upstream deprecated-parameter warning; the installed typed API exposes only the zero-argument initializer.

primaryInput.action: tap once near the center of the portrait game frame
primaryInput.observed: the real knife reaches the wall blade-first, individual courses begin splitting, colored cap faces appear, and each accepted course emits +1

win.action: tap once and allow the opening wall sequence to complete
win.observed: score and best reach seven, exactly seven physical courses are removed, untouched lower courses remain, and colored halves settle around the course

loss.action: stage an isolated handle-only target approach and advance the deterministic simulation by 200ms
loss.observed: score remains zero, no target splits, and the knife bounces upward and backward away from the intact target
